clue.text: Tiny creature makes vet lose heart

indicators.note: the vetting verb must give up its central letter, the single letter at its very heart

parts.note: to vet something is to check it over, to inspect it

explanation.surface: A vet's patient is so small that the vet despairs of treating it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose heart' takes the middle letter P out of INSPECT, the seven-letter verb meaning vet. 'makes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug or beetle is a small six-legged animal, so a tiny creature in the everyday sense.

clue.text: How stupid am I, to be keeping rising parasites

parts.note: am I, put the other way round, is the contraction I'm

indicators.note: the verb be keeps the reversed parasites inside it

parts.note: to be gives the verb be

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for parasites reads upwards

parts.note: lice are parasitic insects

explanation.surface: Someone berates himself for being foolish enough to keep breeding lice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' (upwards in a down clue) turns the parasites round, and 'keeping' wraps 'be' around them. 'How' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbecile as an adjective means foolish or idiotic.

clue.text: Bow's used the wrong way by fiddler

definitions.text: Bow's used the wrong way by fiddler

parts.words: Bow's used the wrong way by fiddler
parts.note: an incompetent violinist drags the bow so that the strings grate and screech, earning a disparaging name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' suggests bowing and scraping, a deferential bow; here it is a violin bow, used so badly the playing grates.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor violinist is mocked as one who scrapes the strings, a crude fiddler.

clue.text: Accident almost involving foreigner's vehicle

indicators.note: the shortened accident word wraps around the foreigner
almost means the word for accident stops just short of its final letter

parts.note: chance means accident, as in by chance
an Arab is a crossword stock foreigner

explanation.surface: A foreign tourist's coach nearly crashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of the accident word, and 'involving' wraps what is left around the foreigner. A charabanc was a motor coach for day trips.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old open motor coach used for outings.

clue.text: In fight, not having to lose consciousness

indicators.note: the word for 'not having' is placed in the word for fight

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match or contest
to lack something is not to have it

explanation.surface: A boxer in a bout is knocked so hard that he faints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' wraps the fight around 'not having'; 'to' just joins the wordplay to the definition, which is a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To black out is the idiom for fainting, passing out.

clue.text: Get cross, having seen some petrol spilt

indicators.note: spilt suggests the letters are scattered about and gathered into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A motorist gets angry after watching fuel being spilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' rearranges the fourteen letters of SEEN SOME PETROL; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To get cross is to become angry, the idiom being to lose your composure.

clue.text: Measure how to make ten thousand, say

indicators.note: say signals that the instruction is spoken, matching the measure in sound

parts.note: how to turn ten into a thousand: cube it, since ten times ten times ten is a thousand

explanation.surface: A puzzle asks how a measurement might reach ten thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'ten thousand' as turning ten into a thousand: the instruction is 'cube it', which spoken matches the measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubit is an ancient length measure, roughly a forearm long.

clue.text: Blanket — it provides protection

definitions.meaning: blanket as an adjective means all-embracing, total
a loose protective work garment worn over clothes

explanation.surface: A blanket keeps you safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanket coverage is total and comprehensive; and a smock-like coat shields clothes from dirt.

clue.text: There were seven against this article, but eight supporters, initially

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A historical note about seven attackers and eight defenders of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seven Against Thebes' is Aeschylus's tragedy about seven champions attacking the Greek city; BES are the first letters of 'but eight supporters'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek city was attacked by seven champions in the Aeschylus play.

clue.text: Job only rancher can create, producing malt liquor

indicators.note: the letters can create a new phrase when rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A rancher's only job is brewing beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can create' rearranges JOB ONLY RANCHER; 'producing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk name personifies barley and the ale or whisky distilled or brewed from it.

clue.text: It's cruel using spur endlessly on horse

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a Barb is a breed of North African horse

indicators.note: the verb for spur loses its final letter, cut off at the end

parts.note: to spur someone on is to stir or arouse them

explanation.surface: A rider is being cruel by digging spurs into a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the spur verb, and 'on' (across) puts the result after the horse. 'It's' and 'using' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarous behaviour is savage and brutal, so cruel.

clue.text: The old note part of speech that's about the close of life

indicators.note: about means the grammatical word is turned round

parts.note: a verb is one of the grammatical parts of speech

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a grammatical term concerning the end of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns VERB into BREV; 'the close of life' gives E. 'that's' is a link. The note was used in older music, worth two semibreves.
explanation.definitionFit: This long note, twice a semibreve, is rarely seen in modern scores, hence old.

clue.text: Leader showing panic at disorder

indicators.note: putting the letters of the preceding words into disorder rearranges them

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A leader reveals his panic when chaos breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' rearranges the seven letters of PANIC AT; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain commands a team or ship, so is its head.

clue.text: Silver involved in bizarre offence

indicators.note: the symbol for silver is wrapped up within the word meaning bizarre

parts.note: outré means eccentric or bizarre
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Stolen silver is caught up in a strange crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' places the silver symbol between the R and E of the French-derived word for bizarre; 'Silver' looks like a person or metal in a crime story.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is anger at an affront, and also the affront itself, a gross offence.

clue.text: Grub in spectacular variety

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: A grub appears in a dazzling variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'spectacuLAR VAriety'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the soft young stage of an insect, before it pupates.

clue.text: During walk, girl is open to suggestion

indicators.note: the girl comes during the walk, so her name goes inside it

parts.note: to amble is to walk at a leisurely pace
Ena is a girl's name, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: On a stroll, a girl is happy to take advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' puts the girl inside the walk; 'is' is a link. Ena is a stock crossword girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amenable is willing and compliant, ready to go along with ideas.

clue.text: Completely change one's views on the subject of sauce

parts.note: about means concerning, on the subject of
sauce and face both mean cheek, impudence

explanation.surface: Someone does a complete U-turn in a debate over a condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' means impudence, as does 'face' (the brass neck to do something).
explanation.definitionFit: An about-face is a reversal of opinion, originally a military turn.

clue.text: But we're told where this carriage ended

definitions.text: But we're told where this carriage ended

parts.words: But we're told where this carriage ended
parts.note: 'But we're told' signals a sound-alike for butt, the wine cask in which Shakespeare's George, brother of Edward IV, was drowned in malmsey; the duke's title is also a type of carriage

explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Richard III the Duke is drowned in a butt (cask) of malmsey; his title also names a closed four-wheeled carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The ducal title names a four-wheeled closed carriage, and the duke famously died in a wine cask.

clue.text: A couple rented jewelry

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
let means rented out, as in a flat to let

explanation.surface: Two people hired some jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bangle or chain worn on the wrist is a piece of personal adornment.

clue.text: Give more consideration to the changes accepted by bowlers

indicators.note: the rearranged word is taken in by the bowling team

parts.note: a rink is a team of four players in lawn bowls

indicators.note: changes means the letters of the little word are moved around

explanation.surface: Bowlers agree to changes after giving them more thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges 'the', and 'accepted by' places it in the bowls team. 'bowlers' suggests cricket, but in lawn bowls a team is a rink.
explanation.definitionFit: To rethink a plan is to reconsider it, think again.

clue.text: Yellow flowers in a ring around window

parts.note: or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow

indicators.note: around means the garland word is turned the other way

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland, a ring of flowers

explanation.surface: Yellow blooms sit in a circle round a window frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the garland word round. 'flowers' tempts as plants alone, but 'flowers in a ring' is the Hawaiian garland.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a bay window projecting from an upper storey.

clue.text: A country — North America, or part of it

parts.note: India is a country

explanation.surface: A quiz question asks whether a place is a country or part of a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to North America: the definition is a part of that continent. 'A' and 'or' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a Midwestern US state, so a portion of the continent.

clue.text: Companion of Cortes, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the name might be rearranged into another word

parts.note: the conquistador's name supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A question about who travelled with the conquistador Cortés.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CORTES; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort accompanies someone, a partner or guide.

clue.text: Content if stays are tight

indicators.note: tight means drunk, so the words reel about into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A corset fits nicely if its stays are pulled tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are tight' rearranges IF STAYS. 'Content' is the verb, as in content oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To content someone is to please them, to meet their wishes.

clue.text: Stitch holds in tendon

indicators.note: the sewing word holds the little word inside it

parts.note: to stitch is to sew

explanation.surface: A surgeon's stitch keeps a tendon in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts the clue's own 'in' inside the stitching verb; 'Stitch' as a noun suggests surgery, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinew is a tough band of tissue joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Gypsy holds information about one fighting in the ring

indicators.note: about means the whole assembly is turned round
the Gypsy word holds the information word inside it

parts.note: a Rom is a Romany man, a Gypsy
data are facts or information

explanation.surface: A Romany fortune-teller has inside knowledge of a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts the information inside the Gypsy, and 'about' then turns the whole assembly round, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull, in the bullring.

clue.text: Hunter bags head of oryx, reebok and impala outside Nairobi

indicators.note: the head of each word is its first letter, taken from each of the five words that follow

explanation.surface: A big-game hunter shoots antelope on the outskirts of the Kenyan capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' applies to all five words, including 'outside', which looks like an instruction but is just another word supplying its initial. 'bags' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the giant huntsman was placed among the stars as a constellation.

clue.text: Love girl to win a second time

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like an O
Vera is a girl's name
to gain something is to win it

explanation.surface: A lover hopes to win his girlfriend back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something over again means repeating it, once more.

clue.text: You and I about to be beset by attractive fly

indicators.note: the reversed pronoun is surrounded by the word for attractive

parts.note: taking means charming or attractive

indicators.note: about means the two-person pronoun is turned round

parts.note: you and I together are we

explanation.surface: Two people are about to be pestered by an annoying insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the pronoun round and 'beset by' surrounds it with the attractive word. 'to be' is a link; 'fly' looks like the insect but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To take wing is the idiom for taking to the air, flying off.

clue.text: Cave comes to mind

definitions.meaning: cave is Latin for look out, schoolboy slang shouted as a warning
mind as a warning, as in mind the step

explanation.surface: A cavern brings back memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave' reads as a cavern, but it is the Latin warning (said KAY-vee) used at British public schools; 'comes to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are warnings to take care, the Latin imperative and the English imperative.
